new.title: Rank bounds the number of distinct nonconstant edge coordinates after prescribed graph edges are contracted
new.unlocks: bounds the number of distinct nonconstant edge-coordinate functions in a graph with a bounded number of cuts
new.context: Contract the prescribed edges. Nonconstant edge coordinates are exactly the distinct unordered pairs of different contracted vertices joined by an edge. A connected component on s+1 vertices contributes s bits of cut rank and at most s(s+1)/2 distinct pairs. Independent component flips give exactly 2 to the total rank many cut patterns. Sum these bounds and use superadditivity of the triangular numbers. Allow at least 60 minutes.

new.title: An existential choice of witness bits gives an exact effective rank for adaptive binary parity queries
new.statement:
∀ (m h q : Nat),
  let U := Fin h → ZMod 2
  let V := Fin m → ZMod 2
  let moves := min h (q-1)
  let cap := 2^moves * (q-moves)
  let feasible := fun (label : U → V → Bool) =>
    ∃ (ask : (j : Fin q) → (Fin j.val → ZMod 2) → ((U × V) →ₗ[ZMod 2] ZMod 2))
      (answers : U → V → Fin q → ZMod 2) (leaf : (Fin q → ZMod 2) → Bool),
      (∀ (u : U) (x : V) (j : Fin q), answers u x j =
        ask j (fun i => answers u x ⟨i.val, Nat.lt_trans i.isLt j.isLt⟩) (u,x)) ∧
      ∀ (u : U) (x : V), label u x = leaf (answers u x)
  (∀ label : U → V → Bool, feasible label → (∀ u, label u 0 = false) →
    ∃ A : V →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin cap → ZMod 2),
      ∀ (u : U) (x : V), label u x = true → A x ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ A : V →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin cap → ZMod 2),
    ∃ label : U → V → Bool, feasible label ∧
      ∀ x : V, (∃ u : U, label u x = true) ↔ A x ≠ 0)
new.unlocks: determines how many independent feature directions can be detected by a bounded adaptive parity tree with fully available witness copies
new.context: Follow every transcript attained on the zero feature as the witness varies. A fresh witness parity splits the node. At a forced node subtract the same combination of earlier queries that cancels its witness coefficients, leaving one feature parity. Features killing every resulting parity can never leave the zero-feature tree. Its forced-node count is at most 2^t(q−t). Conversely read t witness bits as an address and ask the q−t feature parities stored there. Estimate 2 to 4 hours.

new.title: Exact key counts for stopped row-guard prefixes and equal output fibers of path-dependent dimension through the penultimate round
new.statement:
∀ (k r d i : Nat), 6 ≤ r → k + 3 + d = 5 * r →
  let n := r - 5
  d ≤ n → i < k → i + (n - d) ≤ k →
  ∀ (u : Fin (2 ^ k)) (constant : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k)),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc j =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit j)
        (!(word.testBit ((j + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((j + 2) % k))).toNat <<< j)) 0
  let state := fun (rounds key : Nat) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev t =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * t) key ^^^
        (constant (t + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ u.val)
  let q := k + i + 3 * r - d
  let trace := fun (len key : Nat) =>
    ((List.range len).foldl (fun (posCode : Nat × Nat) idx =>
      let pos := posCode.1 - 2
      let prev := state (idx + 4) key
      let hit := xor (xor (prev.testBit (pos % k)) (prev.testBit ((pos + 1) % k)))
        (prev.testBit ((pos + 2) % k))
      (pos - (if hit then 0 else 1), posCode.2 ||| (hit.toNat <<< idx)))
      (q - 13, 0)).2
  ∀ (len : Nat) (code : Fin (2 ^ len)), len ≤ n →
    let wt := fun (count : Nat) =>
      ((List.range count).filter (fun digit => code.val.testBit digit)).length
    (len = 0 ∨ d < wt (len - 1) + (n + 1 - len)) →
    let keys := (List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun raw => trace len raw == code.val)
    keys.length = 2 ^ (k - len) ∧
      (len = n → d < wt len →
        let m := wt len - d
        ∀ target : Fin (2 ^ m),
          (keys.filter (fun candidate =>
            ((state r candidate >>> i) % 2 ^ m) == target.val)).length = 2 ^ (k - n - m))
new.unlocks: counts each reachable prefix and each terminal output block
new.context: On paper. Each live guard has a linear leftmost starting bit strictly left of all preceding guard supports. Solve these bits in order. On a full path with S>d ones every guard also misses the eventual block of S-d hidden bits, even modulo k. Compare keys differing on a prefix of this block. The moving interval covers the final update and earlier injections miss the changed prefix. Its last injection determines the highest hidden bit. Solve the block downwards. Allow at least 60 minutes.

new.title: A common-key circuit priced by the binomial sum for variable-length recovery at cyclic widths k=5r-3-d
new.statement:
∀ (k r d : Nat), 6 ≤ r → d ≤ r - 5 → k + 3 + d = 5 * r →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let h := (k + 1) / 2
  let graph : Fin (2 ^ k) → Fin (2 ^ k) → Bool := fun row col =>
    (List.range (2 ^ k)).any (fun w =>
      decide (first w row.val < 2 ^ (k - h)) && decide (second w col.val < 2 ^ (k - h)))
  let n := r - 5
  let slots := ((List.range (n + 1)).map (fun successes =>
    Nat.choose n successes * 2 ^ (k - n - (successes - d)))).sum
  ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (k + k) C ∧
    C.size ≤ 128 * (k + 1) ^ 2 * (r + 1) * slots ∧
    ∀ bits : Fin (k + k) → Bool,
      C.eval (List.ofFn bits) = PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) graph bits
new.unlocks: bounds the gates for finding a key that passes both full tests
new.context: On paper. Give a stopped length-a prefix one slot for each of its 2^(k-a) free assignments. All virtual extensions have at most d ones, so those slots have exactly their combined binomial charge. On complete paths solve the chronological guard pivots and then max(0,j-d) row pivots downwards. A zero probe recovers each pivot using the input row. Test both full states on that key and OR the slots. At most k+2 state evaluations per slot fit the gate budget. Allow at least 60 minutes.

new.title: At least two AND/OR gates per row if every pair of rows shares a column missed by any designated third row
new.statement:
∀ (n m s : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool),
  3 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v w : Fin n, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost G s →
  2 * n ≤ s
new.unlocks: gives a row gate bound for every bipartite graph satisfying the triple condition
new.context: Three rows have a witness column for each missed row, forcing six gates. Induct by two-gate row deletion or use one binary row OR per input. Incomparability makes these ORs distinct and prevents one reading another. A shared sole reader cannot be OR by domination. For AND, take a column meeting both rows and missing a third. The partner operand would be on and off with just that column on. Each row OR can therefore charge two slots in readers outside the row ORs. Fixed-size companions cannot exist: at n=3 repeat all three witness columns many times, forcing unbounded column reads.

new.title: Sparse paired graphs realize every covered set of asymmetric pairs with one NOT and at most one additional read per exposed raw input
new.statement:
∀ (n d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (mate rank : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))
    (rows cols : Finset (Fin n)),
  let A := fun (i j : Fin n) => G i (mate j)
  let cover := ∀ i j, A i j = true → A j i = false →
    i ∈ rows ∨ j ∈ cols ∨ j ∈ rows ∨ i ∈ cols
  (∀ v : Fin n, (Finset.univ.filter (fun later : Fin n =>
    rank v < rank later ∧ (A v later = true ∨ A later v = true))).card ≤ d) →
  (cover ↔ ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (2 * n) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C ∧
    PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C ≤ 1 ∧
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = .not → g.inputs.length = 1) ∧
    2 * n ≤ C.output ∧ C.output < 2 * n + C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ n + 24 * (n + 1) * (d + 1) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n,
      (∃ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = .or ∧
        (g.inputs = [i.val, n + (mate i).val] ∨
         g.inputs = [n + (mate i).val, i.val])) ∧
      (C.gates.map (fun g => g.inputs.count i.val)).sum ≤
        1 + (if i ∈ rows then 1 else 0) ∧
      (C.gates.map (fun g => g.inputs.count (n + (mate i).val))).sum ≤
        1 + (if i ∈ cols then 1 else 0))
new.unlocks: gives the actual circuit price for covered asymmetric pairs with bounded forward degree
new.context: On paper. An uncovered asymmetric pair gives two indistinguishable crossed inputs. Start H with the monotone absent-pair test. Add the two-signal upper set of each negative asymmetric cell above a positive. Positive profiles above H have no negative above them, since that would require four strictly nested profiles, or a positive on an absent pair. OR their upper sets with those of remaining positives guarded by NOT H. There are at most n+2nd terms. Buffer each allowed raw once and include the n paired ORs in the gate count. Allow at least 60 minutes.

new.title: A full record of two-round guard answers determines its queried starting bits and the exact number of cyclic keys
new.statement:
∀ (k a : Nat), 6 ≤ k → ∀ (anchor : Fin k) (u : Fin (2 ^ k))
    (constant : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k)) (code : Fin (10 ^ a)),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc j =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit j)
        (!(word.testBit ((j + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((j + 2) % k))).toNat <<< j)) 0
  let state := fun (rounds key : Nat) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev tick =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * tick) key ^^^
        (constant (tick + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ u.val)
  let injected := fun (round key pos : Nat) =>
    xor ((rot (2 * (round - 1)) key).testBit (pos % k))
      ((constant round).val.testBit (pos % k))
  let bit := fun (round key pos : Nat) => (state round key).testBit (pos % k)
  let guard := fun (round key stop : Nat) =>
    xor (xor (bit round key (stop - 2)) (bit round key (stop - 1))) (bit round key stop)
  let branch := fun (t edge subject : Nat) =>
    let hit := guard (t - 1) subject edge
    let mid := edge - 3 + hit.toNat
    let next := guard t subject mid
    if hit then
      let near := bit t subject (edge - 2) ==
        xor (injected t subject (edge - 1)) (injected t subject edge)
      let far := bit t subject (edge - 3) == injected t subject edge
      2 + near.toNat + 2 * far.toNat + 4 * next.toNat
    else next.toNat
  let gain := fun (v : Nat) =>
    if v < 2 then v else 1 + (v - 2) / 4 + (if v = 9 then 1 else 0)
  let q := anchor.val + (10 * a + 30) * k
  let trace := fun (len keyWord : Nat) =>
    (List.range len).foldl (fun (acc : Nat × Nat) j =>
      let v := branch (5 + 2 * j) acc.1 keyWord
      (acc.1 - 6 + gain v, acc.2 + v * 10 ^ j)) (q - 13, 0)
  let digit := fun (j : Nat) => (code.val / 10 ^ j) % 10
  let total := fun (a : Nat) => ((List.range a).map (fun h => gain (digit h))).sum
  let queried := (List.range a).flatMap (fun pairNo =>
    let t := 5 + 2 * pairNo
    let edge := q - 13 - 6 * pairNo + total pairNo
    let pivot := edge + 3 - 2 * t
    if digit pairNo < 2 then [pivot, pivot - 5]
    else [pivot, pivot - 2, pivot - 3, pivot - 4])
  let hidden := queried.map (fun lifted => lifted % k)
  (a = 0 ∨ 25 + 10 * (a - 1) ≤ k + total (a - 1)) →
    (∀ visible : Fin (2 ^ k), ∃! candidate : Fin (2 ^ k),
      (trace a candidate.val).2 = code.val ∧
      ∀ place : Fin k, place.val ∉ hidden →
        (rot 1 candidate.val ^^^ u.val).testBit place.val = visible.val.testBit place.val) ∧
    ((List.range (2 ^ k)).filter (fun trial => (trace a trial).2 == code.val)).length =
      2 ^ (k - queried.length)
new.unlocks: counts keys with each eligible complete record by reconstructing all queried pivots
new.context: On paper. The six-bit windows shift left by ten minus the gain, at least seven. Freshness at the last parent puts every earlier window in the same period. Set the free starting bits. Reconstruct each digit by its two or four zero probes. Later pivots lie below the current leftmost read, and truncation at q removes their upper aliases. Each digit forces its pivots. Invert the starting rotation to obtain the key. Counting the distinct free assignments also covers the empty record and a last failing digit. Allow 30 to 90 minutes.

new.title: Finite two-sided bounds on the slot price of a three-state gain scan at arbitrary depths
new.statement:
let move := fun (mode letter : Nat) =>
    let aligned := ((mode == 1) && letter.testBit 0 && letter.testBit 1) ||
      ((mode == 2) && letter.testBit 1)
    let hit := letter.testBit 2
    (if aligned then (if hit then 0 else 2) else 1,
      hit.toNat + (aligned && hit).toNat)
  let summary := fun (code length : Nat) =>
    (List.range length).foldl (fun (st : Nat × Nat) digitPos =>
      let result := move st.1 ((code >>> (3 * digitPos)) % 8)
      (result.1, st.2 + result.2)) (0, 0)
  let price := fun (n depth : Nat) =>
    ((List.range (8 ^ n)).map (fun codeWord =>
      2 ^ (2 * n - ((summary codeWord n).2 - depth)))).sum
  ∀ (n d : Nat), 0 < n →
    let deficit := 5 * n - 8 * d
    let blocks := 1 + 128 * deficit ^ 2 / n
    2 ^ (5 * n) ≤ 2 ^ (12 * blocks) * price n d ∧
      2 ^ (deficit ^ 2 / (200 * n)) * price n d ≤ 2 ^ (5 * n + 1)
new.unlocks: bounds the finite normalized slot price above and below at every positive length
new.context: On paper. For D>0 tilt the compensated sum with lambda=D/(100n). The chord bound for exp on [-10,10] and conditional mean zero give a moment factor at most exp(50 lambda²) per step. This bounds the price from above. For the lower bound partition into B near-equal blocks when B≤n. From every incoming mode each block has chance ≥2^-12 to drop by sqrt(length)/8. Together the drops cover D, forcing full price. If B>n, take words with every hit bit zero. Allow at least 60 minutes.

new.title: The transcript and nonpivot bits of the greedy row scan give a bijection from accepting keys to binomial-tail addresses
new.statement:
∀ (k r e q : ℕ) (constants : ℕ → Fin (2 ^ k)) (u i : ℕ),
  0 < q → 3 * e + 2 * q + 3 ≤ r → k + e + 3 = 5 * r → u < 2 ^ k → i < k →
  let cut := e + q + 3
  let N := r - e - cut
  let D := e + q - 1
  let m := N - D
  let rot := fun (s wordR : ℕ) =>
    ((wordR <<< (s % k)) ||| (wordR >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun w : ℕ => (List.range k).foldl (fun v b =>
    v ||| ((xor (w.testBit b)
      (!(w.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && w.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
  let state := fun (key rounds : ℕ) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev t =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^
        rot (2 * t) key ^^^ (constants (t + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ u)
  let evenCount := fun tr : List (ℕ × Bool) => (tr.filter (fun item => !item.2)).length
  let scan := fun subject : ℕ =>
    (List.range N).foldl (fun (cfg : Bool × List (ℕ × Bool)) ix =>
      let tr₀ := cfg.2
      let zeros := evenCount tr₀
      let ones := tr₀.length - zeros
      if cfg.1 || decide (m ≤ zeros ∨ D < ones) then cfg
      else
        let t₀ := cut + ix + 1
        let g := D - ones
        if 4 * (r - t₀) < g then (true, tr₀)
        else
          let z := state subject (t₀ - 1)
          let b₀ := (i + 3 * r + k - (3 * t₀ + g)) % k
          let oddGuard := xor (xor (z.testBit b₀) (z.testBit ((b₀ + 1) % k)))
            (z.testBit ((b₀ + 2) % k))
          let pivot := (i + 3 * r + k + 5 - (5 * t₀ + g)) % k
          (false, tr₀ ++ [(pivot, oddGuard)]))
      (false, [])
  let accepted := fun keyA : ℕ =>
    let result := scan keyA
    result.1 = false ∧ evenCount result.2 = m
  let encode := fun keyE : ℕ =>
    let trace := (scan keyE).2
    let pivots := trace.map Prod.fst
    let x := rot 1 keyE ^^^ u
    let rest := ((List.range k).filter (fun freeBit => decide (freeBit ∉ pivots))).map (fun p => x.testBit p)
    ((trace.map Prod.snd) ++ rest).foldr (fun bit acc => bit.toNat + 2 * acc) 0
  Set.BijOn encode {raw : ℕ | raw < 2 ^ k ∧ accepted raw}
    {addr : ℕ | addr < 2 ^ k ∧ ((Finset.range N).filter (fun lowBit => addr.testBit lowBit)).card ≤ D}
new.unlocks: identifies the exact low-weight addresses for reaching the required number of zero guards
new.context: Read the low N address bits through zero number m. With f≤D ones and fewer than m zeros, the next trial has 0≤g=D−f≤N−s≤4(r−t). The prefix determines the pivots and 5t+g rises by four or five. Fill the other starting bits in order from the rest of the address. Apply the mixed-target inverse, undo rotation and row XOR. The scan follows those answers and stops at the chosen zero. Encoding returns the address. In the other direction the observed prefix and nonpivots determine the original key. Count addresses by low-word weight. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: A triangular list of Boolean products has an exact Walsh coefficient product on its independent operand inputs
changed.statement:
∀ s : ℕ,
  let V := Fin s → ZMod 2
  let dot := fun (u v : V) => ∑ i : Fin s, u i * v i
  let sign := fun (x : ZMod 2) => if x = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  ∀ (A B : Fin s → Fin s → ZMod 2) (γ : V) (Z : V → V → V),
  (∀ x y i, Z x y i =
    (x i + ∑ j ∈ Finset.Iio i, A i j * Z x y j) *
    (y i + ∑ j ∈ Finset.Iio i, B i j * Z x y j)) →
  ∀ p q : V,
    let c := fun (j : Fin s) =>
      γ j + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ioi j, (p i * A i j + q i * B i j)
    (∑ x : V, ∑ y : V, sign (dot γ (Z x y) + dot p x + dot q y)) =
      ∏ j : Fin s,
        if c j = 0 then (if p j = 0 ∧ q j = 0 then 4 else 0)
        else 2 * sign (p j * q j)

changed.context: Use the actual pair of operands at every product as coordinates U_i,V_i. Recover each raw bit from its actual operand by adding the specified earlier products U_j V_j. This triangular change is a bijection. In the Walsh exponent, collect the coefficient of U_j V_j from the output and all later frequency terms. Each remaining summand involves only one pair. Factor the finite sum and evaluate the four input assignments of a single pair. Gate-price companions cannot exist for this character sum. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: Exact field-linear scan dimension for counting cyclic window solutions in the best fixed table order
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (a w d : ℕ),
  let n := a + 2
  let Table := (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool
  let count := fun (T : Fin n → Table) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Bool)).filter (fun x =>
      ∀ i : Fin n, T i (fun j => x (Fin.ofNat (a + 2) (i.val + j.val))) = true)).card
  (∃ (order : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (s : Fin d → K)
      (step : Fin n → Table → (Fin d → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin d → K))
      (out : (Fin d → K) →ₗ[K] K),
    ∀ T : Fin n → Table,
      out ((List.finRange n).foldl (fun v j => step j (T (order j)) v) s) =
        (count T : K)) ↔
    2 ^ min n (2 * w) ≤ d
changed.unlocks: determines the minimum dimension of a fixed-order field-linear counter for arbitrary cyclic window tables
changed.context: A prefix vector and suffix functional factor the cut matrix. Local singleton pins give identity on assignments shared by both sides. Color the row starts by side. In each cyclic run of length b its initial min(w,b) sites see both colors among their preceding w+1 starts including themselves. At a half cut their total is at least min(n,2w). Natural order has two runs and never exceeds that bound. Keep counts by shared assignment, updating linearly by matching old bits and summing newly forgotten ones. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a field-coordinate dimension. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: Exact linear scan dimension for counting cyclic words with reversible binary feedback in physical row order
changed.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (b : ℕ),
  let w := b + 1
  let D := 2 ^ w
  let threshold := if ringChar K = 2 then (D - 2) ^ 2 else (D - 1) ^ 2 + 1
  let Control := (Fin b → Bool) → Bool
  ∀ (a m : ℕ),
    let n := a + 1
    let count := fun (C : Fin n → Control) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Bool)).filter (fun x =>
        ∀ i : Fin n,
          x (Fin.ofNat (a + 1) (i.val + w)) =
            xor (x i) (C i (fun j => x (Fin.ofNat (a + 1) (i.val + 1 + j.val)))))).card
    let admits :=
      ∃ (s : Fin m → K)
        (step : Fin n → Control → (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K))
        (out : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] K),
        ∀ C : Fin n → Control,
          out ((List.finRange n).foldl (fun v i => step i (C i) v) s) = (count C : K)
    (threshold ≤ m → admits) ∧ (8 * w ≤ n → admits → threshold ≤ m)

changed.context: Each control permutes the D seeds. The word count is the fixed-point count of their product. Track the product on the zero-sum space modulo its constant vectors and retain a constant coordinate when its trace correction is nonzero. At a cut after 4w rows each half can realize every seed permutation by reversible routing. Extra rows can rotate, with the routed permutation compensating. Prefix states and suffix functionals therefore factor the full fixed-point count matrix through the scan dimension. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt, integral normalized Walsh coefficients characterize uniform probability weights on affine binary subspaces
changed.statement:
∀ d : ℕ,
  let V := Fin d → ZMod 2
  let dot := fun (a x : V) => ∑ i, a i * x i
  let spin := fun (a x : V) => if dot a x = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  ∀ F : V → ℕ, (∑ x, F x) = 2^d →
    ((∀ a : V, (2^d : ℤ) ∣ ∑ x : V, (F x : ℤ) * spin a x) ↔
      ∃ (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) V) (z : V),
        ∀ x : V, F x = @ite ℕ (∀ a ∈ U, dot a x = dot a z)
          (Classical.propDecidable _) (2^(Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U)) 0)

changed.context: Normalize by the total mass. Each integer coefficient is zero or ±1. A coefficient has modulus one exactly when its character is constant on the positive support. Those characters form a linear subspace. Evaluate their signs at any support point, then use Walsh inversion and character orthogonality. Conversely the sum of a character on an affine subspace is zero or its signed cardinality. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: Every minimum OR decoder has exactly r minus one laminar gate supports inside each signed r-literal target
changed.statement:
∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
  let S := Fin (2 * r)
  let names := fun (x : Fin (2 ^ r)) =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun i : S => Nat.testBit x.val (i.val / 2) = decide (i.val % 2 = 1))
  let supp := fun (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (w : ℕ) =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun i : S =>
      (D.wires (List.ofFn (fun h : S => decide (h = i)))).getD w false = true)
  let realizes := fun (D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ D.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧ g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    ∀ x : Fin (2 ^ r), ∃ w : ℕ, supp D w = names x
  ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, realizes C →
    (∀ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, realizes D → C.size ≤ D.size) →
    ∀ x : Fin (2 ^ r),
      let support := fun (g : Fin C.size) => supp C (2 * r + g.val)
      let I := Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Fin C.size => support g ⊆ names x)
      I.card + 1 = r ∧ ∀ p ∈ I, ∀ q ∈ I,
        Disjoint (support p) (support q) ∨ support p ⊆ support q ∨ support q ⊆ support p
changed.unlocks: Restricts the support families that can occur at exact budget when testing optimal signed name encoders.
changed.context: Use the pruned binary tree for each target in the split bound. A gate with t compatible literals can occur only on its 2^(r-t) extensions. In each tree its branch charge is at most 2^t. Averaging bounds every gate by one. The split construction attains the least tree charge. Thus in a minimum circuit every gate occurs on every extension and its support equals its descendant leaves there. Each tree has r-1 branches, whose leaf sets are nested or disjoint.

changed.title: A ternary cyclic table encoding with the minimum visible literal count
changed.statement:
∀ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n),
  let V := Sum (Fin n) (Fin n × (Fin (w + 1) → Bool))
  let accepts := fun (a : V → Bool) =>
    ∀ i : Fin n, a (Sum.inr (i, fun j : Fin (w + 1) =>
      a (Sum.inl ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩))) = true
  letI : DecidableEq V := Classical.typeDecidableEq V
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    letI : DecidableEq (Sum V (Fin m)) := Classical.typeDecidableEq _
    m + (∑ D ∈ F, D.card) + 3*n ≤ (8*n+1)*2^n + 2*n*2^(min n (w+1)) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin n) (b : Bool),
      (F.filter (fun D => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl i), b) ∈ D)).card = 1) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin n) (p : Fin (w+1) → Bool),
      (F.filter (fun D => (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (i,p)), false) ∈ D)).card = 0 ∧
      (F.filter (fun D => (Sum.inl (Sum.inr (i,p)), true) ∈ D)).card =
        (if ∃ x : Fin n → Bool, ∀ j : Fin (w+1), x ⟨(i.val+j.val)%n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ = p j then 1 else 0)) ∧
    (∀ D ∈ F, D.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ a : V → Bool, accepts a ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim a aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ ρ : V → Option Bool,
      let assumptions : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ v : V, l.1 = Sum.inl v ∧ ρ v = some l.2}
      let completion := fun (a : V → Bool) =>
        accepts a ∧ ∀ (v : V) (b : Bool), ρ v = some b → a v = b
      ((¬ ∃ a : V → Bool, completion a) ↔
        ∃ D ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ D, PEqualNP.Search.UPForces (↑F : Set _) assumptions
          (PEqualNP.Search.negLit l)) ∧
      ((∃ a : V → Bool, completion a) → ∀ (v : V) (b : Bool),
        (∀ a : V → Bool, completion a → a v = b) ↔
          PEqualNP.Search.UPForces (↑F : Set _) assumptions (Sum.inl v, b))

changed.title: Three uncovered positive cells defeat an output-dependent parity exactly by one lost cell or by three lines at one name
changed.statement:
∀ (n names : Nat),
  let V := Fin n → ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (n+1) → ZMod 2
  let E := Fin names × V
  let lift := fun p : E => Fin.cons (1 : ZMod 2) p.2
  let spanAt := fun (cell : Finset E) (y : Fin names) =>
    Submodule.span (ZMod 2) (((cell.filter (fun p => p.1 = y)).image lift : Finset W) : Set W)
  ∀ (negative : Finset E) (positive : Fin 3 → Finset E),
    let H := spanAt negative
    let G := fun (i : Fin 3) (y : Fin names) => H y ⊔ spanAt (positive i) y
    let line := fun (y : Fin names) (x : W) => H y ⊔ Submodule.span (ZMod 2) ({x} : Set W)
    let exact := ∃ coeff : Fin names → W,
      (∀ p ∈ negative, dotProduct (coeff p.1) (lift p) = 0) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 3, ∃ p ∈ positive i, dotProduct (coeff p.1) (lift p) = 1)
    (¬exact) ↔ ((∃ i : Fin 3, ∀ y : Fin names, G i y = H y) ∨
      ∃ (y : Fin names) (a b : W), a ∉ H y ∧ b ∉ H y ∧ (a+b) ∉ H y ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin 3) (z : Fin names), z ≠ y → G i z = H z) ∧
        G 0 y = line y a ∧ G 1 y = line y b ∧ G 2 y = line y (a+b))
changed.unlocks: Enables the scheduled-row search to recognize all three-column conflicts when no positive column alone forces an error.
changed.context: Quotient each name block by the negative span and take their direct sum. Missing a cell cuts out its annihilator in the dual. Two proper subspaces never cover. If three proper ones cover, their pairwise intersections equal their triple intersection J. Add an exclusive point of the third to a point lying just in the other two. Modulo J each subspace has one nonzero point, since sums from the first two must lie in the third. Dualize the binary plane. Each line has a single-name generator, forcing all three names to agree. See 29d002a807.

changed.title: The density of selector edits inside squares bounds the gate deficit for arbitrary one-hot circuits
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (0 < a ∧ 2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N
  ∀ (T : I → I → Bool) (f g : I → Bool) (A B : Finset I) (q u v : ℕ),
    let F := fun x y : I => xor (x.val.testBit (y.val % r)) (xor (f x) (g y))
    0 < v →
    (∀ i j : I, i ≠ j →
      17+2*(v-1) ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T i z ≠ T j z)).card ∧
      17+2*(v-1) ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I => T z i ≠ T z j)).card) →
    (∀ X Y : Finset I, Disjoint X A → Disjoint Y B → X.card = Y.card →
      ((X ×ˢ Y).filter (fun z => T z.1 z.2 ≠ F z.1 z.2)).card ≤ q*X.card+u) →
    ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, (∀ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
      let e := (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : I × I =>
        C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠ T z.1 z.2)).card
      let b := C.gates.countP (fun gate => gate.inputs.length == 2)
      (32*N-(15*b+54+44*(e/v)+A.card+B.card+4*q+2*a*(N/r)))^2 ≤ 4*(e+u)

The bounded address histogram gives p²≤4(e+u)+(4+4q+2aN/r)p. Square the positive part after subtracting that coefficient and insert the retained-label count.

changed.title: One circuit attains the sparse edit count for every selector shift set while every circuit at the same budget loses a constant fraction
changed.statement:
∀ k a : ℕ, (6 ≤ a ∧ 2*2^a ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let r := 2^a
  let I := Fin N

      (∀ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧

        C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠
          xor (xor (z.1.val.testBit (z.2.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor z.1.val z.2.val ∈ D)))

    ∃ C₀, fits C₀ ∧ ∀ D : Finset ℕ, D ⊆ Finset.range r →
      loss C₀ D = N*D.card ∧ (16 ≤ D.card →
        ∀ C, fits C → N*D.card < 128*loss C D)

changed.statement:
∀ (n r : ℕ) (F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))), 0 < r → r ≤ n →

changed.title: Which binary tag assignments maximize average affine codimension over all permutations
changed.statement:
∀ r : Nat, 2 ≤ r →
  let K := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin r → K
  let dot := fun (u v : V) => ∑ j, u j * v j
  let deficiency := fun (tags : V → V) (p : Equiv.Perm V) =>
    Nat.log 2 ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun normal =>
      ∀ x y : V, dot normal (p x + tags x) = dot normal (p y + tags y))).card
  let score := fun (b : V → V) => ∑ p : Equiv.Perm V, deficiency b p
  ∀ tags : V → V,
    score tags ≤ score id ∧ (score tags = score id ↔ Function.Bijective tags)

changed.context: Count nonzero annihilators by rank-one projection. A nonpermutation tag map has an unbalanced nontrivial character by Walsh inversion, losing 2((q/2)!)² incidences. For permutation tags, replacing 2^c-1 by codimension c loses at most one per two-dimensional annihilator subspace counted. Rank-two projections bound that loss by (q-1)(q-2)4((q/4)!)^4/6, strictly below the missing rank-one count. Reindexing covers all permutation tags.

changed.title: Transversal counting bounds how often a fixed-sum vector rule selects a marked position on permutations
changed.statement:
∀ (m h : Nat),
  let K := ZMod 2
  let U := Fin m → K
  let H := Fin h → K
  let I := U × H
  let W := I → I
  let V := I → K
  let b := 2^m
  let s := 2^h
  let n := b*s
  let unit := fun (i j : I) => if j = i then (1 : K) else 0
  let translate := fun (p : Equiv.Perm I) (u : U) (i : I) =>
    ((p i).1 + u, (p i).2)
  ∀ (P : W → V) (A : V),
    (∀ p : Equiv.Perm I, (∑ u : U, P (translate p u)) = A) →
      let cross := (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm I)).filter (fun p =>
        ∀ u : U, ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun i => (p i).1 = u ∧ A i = 1)).card = 1)
      let bad := (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm I)).filter (fun p =>
        ∀ i : I, (p i).1 = 0 → P (fun j => p j) ≠ unit i)
      cross.card = (if ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun i => A i = 1)).card = b
        then s^b * Nat.factorial b * Nat.factorial (n-b) else 0) ∧
        Nat.factorial n ≤ cross.card + b*bad.card
changed.unlocks: Counts the orbits where a fixed sum permits one selected position at every shift.
changed.context: In a shift orbit the zero-prefix positions run through b disjoint blocks partitioning all positions. If every output is a unit at a currently marked position, their binary sum picks exactly one position per block. Every orbit where A fails this test has at least one bad output. Count the transversal permutations by assigning the b marked positions distinct prefixes, then one suffix per marked position, then bijecting the remaining n-b symbols. If the support size differs from b the count is zero.
